sheets.name: Gaps
rows: Lessons learned have no cycle, owner or record

INR-2 requires an after action report within 10 business days. KSI-INR-AAR has a second part: lessons learned are persistently incorporated. INR-3 covers lessons that change the incident response plan. No requirement covers lessons that change anything else, and none states who tracks them, how often, or where.
Add a sentence to INR-2 that records each lesson as an action with an owner and a due date, and reviews open actions in the quarterly review under INR-4.
I-01 INR-2; I-01 INR-3; I-01 INR-4; KSI-INR-AAR; FRD-PER
Five CNA KSIs have no stated review cycle

Each of these KSIs requires that the resources are persistently reviewed or assessed. CNA-2, CNA-4, CNA-5, CNA-6 and CNA-8 state the configuration rule but no cycle for reviewing it, no owner of the review and no record. CNA-3 is the only CNA requirement that states a cycle (every validation run, and at least every 3 days).
Add one requirement that applies the CNA-3 cycle to the configuration rules in CNA-2, CNA-4, CNA-5, CNA-6 and CNA-8 (decision DQ-002).
I-02 CNA-2; I-02 CNA-3; I-02 CNA-4; I-02 CNA-5; I-02 CNA-6; I-02 CNA-8; KSI-CNA-EIS; KSI-CNA-MAT; KSI-CNA-OFA; KSI-CNA-RNT; KSI-CNA-ULN; FRD-PER; VDR-TFR-MVX; DQ-002
Intended state is not enforced automatically

KSI-CNA-EIS requires automated services that assess machine-based resources and enforce their intended state automatically. CNA-2 treats a resource outside the code as a defect to be removed or brought into code within 5 business days. It names no automated assessment and allows the correction to be manual.
State the automated service that detects drift and restores the declared state, and keep the 5 business day limit for differences it cannot restore. The tool must come from the client (Q-007).

KSI-CNA-MAT has two parts: a minimal attack surface, and minimal lateral movement if a resource is compromised. CNA-4 limits public exposure. No requirement mapped to KSI-CNA-MAT addresses lateral movement. CNA-8 separates tenants' workloads from operations tooling and other trust zones, which may be meant to cover it, but it is mapped only to KSI-CNA-ULN.
If CNA-8 is meant to limit lateral movement, map it to KSI-CNA-MAT and say so in the text. Otherwise add a requirement. Confirm with the client (Q-005).
Recovery plan is not reviewed against the objectives

KSI-RPL-ARP requires that the alignment of the recovery plan with the recovery objectives is persistently reviewed. RPL-3 says the plan is kept in step with the architecture. It does not require a review against the RTO and RPO in RPL-1, and names no owner, cycle or record.
Add a review of the recovery plan against RPL-1, with an owner, a cycle and a record location the client sets.
I-03 RPL-1; I-03 RPL-3; KSI-RPL-ARP; FRD-PER
Change logs are kept but monitoring is not stated

KSI-CMT-LMC requires that changes are logged and monitored. CMT-1 requires the pipeline to log each change. No requirement in POL-CMT states that anyone monitors the log, how often, or what happens when a change did not follow CMT-1 to CMT-6.
Add who monitors the change log, how often, and where the review is recorded (Q-008).
CMT-7 cites rules that apply to Rev5 only

CMT-7 cites FRC-CCL-UCC and FRC-CCL-DCC. In FRMR 2026.11.02.01 these rules sit in the FRC-CCL subset, which applies to Rev5 only. For 20x, the evaluation steps listed under SCN-CSO-EVA say that a change of certification class needs a new assessment and is not handled under the significant change rules. CMT-7 states the same in substance, so only the citation is wrong.
Cite SCN-CSO-EVA in CMT-7 in place of FRC-CCL-UCC and FRC-CCL-DCC.
INR-1, INR-2, CNA-1 to CNA-6, CNA-8, RPL-2 to RPL-5, CMT-1, CMT-2, CMT-4, CMT-6, CMT-7

Each policy names an owner in its header (CISO for POL-INR, Platform Lead for the others). The listed requirements name no role that does the activity. RPL-2 says a failed job alert is acknowledged by a named person but does not say which role. Whether the header owner owns these requirements is not stated.
If the header owner owns every requirement that names no actor, say so once in each policy (decision DQ-001). Name the role that acknowledges RPL-2 alerts.
I-01 INR-1; I-01 INR-2; I-02 CNA-1; I-03 RPL-2; I-03 RPL-3; I-04 CMT-2; FRD-PER; DQ-001
Review and test records have no stated location
INR-3, INR-4, CNA-3, CNA-7a, CNA-7b, RPL-2, RPL-4, CMT-4
These requirements set a cycle but do not say where its record is kept. RPL-1 and CMT-3 do state a record location. A check cannot confirm the status of a cycle without a known record.
State the record location in each requirement (decision DQ-003).
I-01 INR-3; I-01 INR-4; I-02 CNA-3; I-02 CNA-7a; I-02 CNA-7b; I-03 RPL-2; I-03 RPL-4; I-04 CMT-4; I-03 RPL-1; I-04 CMT-3; FRD-PER; VDR-TFR-NMV; DQ-003
Past incident review is owned by a team
INR-4 assigns the quarterly review of past incidents to the security team. A check that compares the reviewer with the policy needs one accountable role. INR-3 names the CISO for the plan review.
Name the role that runs and records the quarterly review (Q-006).
Transformative change review may come after the notices

CNA-7b requires a review of protections before a transformative change starts. SCN-TRF-NIP and SCN-TRF-NFP require notices of initial and final plans 30 and 10 business days before the change starts. A review held just before the start meets CNA-7b but cannot inform those notices.
Set the pre-change review before the final plans notice under SCN-TRF-NFP.
Restore test results are not compared with the objectives

KSI-RPL-TRC requires recovery testing aligned with the recovery objectives. RPL-4 records the time taken and the data age restored, but does not require a comparison with the RTO and RPO in RPL-1 or say what happens when a result falls outside them.
Require the comparison with RPL-1 and record a result outside an objective as a finding.
RPL-5 is mapped to plan alignment but is a scope rule

RPL-5 places the recovery environment under the same scope record and controls as production. That is a scope requirement. It does not address the review of plan alignment that KSI-RPL-ARP requires. RPL-3 is the requirement that maps to KSI-RPL-ARP.
Keep RPL-5, and map it to the scope record rather than to KSI-RPL-ARP.
I-03 RPL-3; I-03 RPL-5; KSI-RPL-ARP; MAS-CSO-IIR
CMT-5 is mapped to procedure review but covers notices
CMT-5 is mapped to KSI-CMT-RVP. It covers the significant change log and notices, not the review of the change procedure. CMT-3 covers KSI-CMT-RVP.
Remove KSI-CMT-RVP from the CMT-5 mapping.

sheets.name: Requirements
rows: The incident response plan defines roles, evaluation steps and the communication timelines for the IEC rules. Each incident is rated with the Potential Agency Impact N-rating (PAIN, N0 to N5) and marked as reportable or not reportable to FedRAMP.
Each FedRAMP Reportable Incident, and each incident rated N2 or above, ends with an after action report within 10 business days. A reportable incident with no rating is treated as N5 (IEC-CSO-DPR).
The CISO reviews the plan each year, and when an after action report or a quarterly incident review finds that the plan needs to change.
each year, and when an after action report or a quarterly incident review finds that the plan needs to change
The security team reviews all past incidents and near misses, of any rating, every quarter for repeated causes. The review lists the incidents it covered and records its findings.

Each resource has a documented function in the scope record and its own role declared in code. A role grants only the named actions its function needs: no wildcard actions, no role shared between services, and permissions unused for 90 days are removed (POL-IAM IAM-3). Network access follows CNA-6, and data access follows SVC-6.
permissions unused for 90 days are removed
Infrastructure is declared in code. A resource that exists outside the code is a defect and is removed or brought into the code within 5 business days.

Each third-party machine-based resource is compared with its provider's best-practice guidance on every validation run, and at least every 3 days: the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark for the AWS account, and the vendor's security baseline for each SaaS tool (E1, E7, E9). Failed controls are fixed or accepted as exceptions under the policy exception process.
on every validation run, and at least every 3 days
Public exposure is limited to the load balancer, gateway and web application firewall (P8). Each open port and public endpoint is justified in the scope record.
scope record (justification of each open port and endpoint)
Production runs in more than one availability zone. Cross-region encrypted backups meet the recovery objectives in policy POL-RPL.
Inbound and outbound traffic is denied by default. Allowed flows match the flows in the scope record.
The Platform Lead reviews protections at least once a year.

The Platform Lead also reviews protections after each change recorded in mas/scope-changes.json. The deadline depends on the change type in the SCN rules. Transformative: before the change starts, and again within 5 business days after it is finished. Adaptive: within 10 business days after the change is finished, before the notice under SCN-ADP-NTF. Not significant: within 20 business days after the change is finished. Routine recurring: no separate review, because the annual review covers these changes.
deadline by SCN change type after each change in mas/scope-changes.json
Production uses logical networks and security groups to separate tenants' workloads from operations tooling and from other trust zones.

The recovery objectives are a recovery time of 8 hours and a recovery point of 4 hours. The Platform Lead reviews them at least every 90 days and records the result in environment/recovery-objectives.json.

Backups run at least every 2 hours, are encrypted and are copied to a second US region (P12) into a vault that has a compliance-mode lock. Backup jobs and copy jobs are monitored every day. A failed job raises an alert within 60 minutes, and a named person acknowledges it.
backups at least every 2 hours; jobs monitored every day; alert within 60 minutes
The recovery plan describes how a recovery environment is built from infrastructure code and how data is restored into it. It is kept in step with the architecture.
A restore test runs at least every 6 months. It records the time taken, the data age restored and any failure.
The recovery environment, once built, falls under the same scope record and controls as production.
Every change to a production resource is made through the pipeline. The pipeline logs the change, the author, the reviewer and the result.
Production machine-based resources are replaced from a trusted image or build. Staff do not modify running resources by hand.
The Platform Lead reviews the change procedure each year, and within 10 business days after any failed or emergency change. Each review is recorded as a new entry in environment/grc-records.json.
each year, and within 10 business days after any failed or emergency change
Every deployment runs automated tests for integrity and security before release and checks that the deployed state matches the intended state after release.
A change that matches a significant change rule is entered in the significant change log. The GRC Lead sends the required notice within the rule timeline (SCN rules).

Every change made through the pipeline is assessed for its change type before release: routine recurring, adaptive, transformative or not significant. Every change gets one of these four types, so no change skips the assessment. Routine recurring and not significant changes need no notice. The type is recorded with the change in the pipeline log (CMT-1), and a change that alters the scope record is also logged in mas/scope-changes.json.
pipeline log; mas/scope-changes.json for scope changes
A change of certification class is not a significant change. It needs a new certification before the offering operates at the new class (FRC-CCL-UCC, FRC-CCL-DCC).
